# FDG9148

> AVOID overloading a method across `Span<T>` and `Memory<T>`, or `ReadOnlySpan<T>` and `ReadOnlyMemory<T>`.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.12 Operating on Buffers.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9148
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Give '{0}', which takes '{1}', a different name from its overload that takes '{2}'

FDG9148 reports an externally visible method that has an externally visible overload in the same type with the same number of parameters, the same ref kinds and the same parameter types, except that at one or more positions it takes Memory<T> where the overload takes Span<T>, or ReadOnlyMemory<T> where the overload takes ReadOnlySpan<T>, with the same T (type parameters of generic methods are compared by position). The report is on the Memory method, the one that can store a reference to the buffer. The exception of the body is not reported: each method returns the type of its own differing parameter, as TrimEnd does when it returns a slice of its input. Overloads inherited from a base type, overrides, interface implementations and overloads that also differ in other parameters are not compared, so coverage is partial. Renaming changes the public API, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.

## From the book

If one overload stores a reference to a buffer and the other operates on it without storing a reference, the methods should have different names.

```csharp
public static void ProcessText(Span<char> span) { ... }
// What's the difference?
public static void ProcessText(Memory<char> memory) { ... }
```

One exception to this guidance is when returning a slice of the input data, where the method returns the input data type, such as a `TrimEnd` method. As noted in earlier guidance, this overload set can be reduced to a single method if the method returns the slice indices instead of the sliced buffer.

```csharp
public static Span<char> TrimEnd(Span<char> span) { ... }
public static Memory<char> TrimEnd(Memory<char> memory) { ... }
```
